Luiza! So you are really going to apply. Good. Ask me anything, because nobody told me the useful things.
Okay. If you were starting your semester in London again tomorrow, what would you do first?
I would sort out my housing before anything else. I waited, and I ended up in a tiny room with a roommate who never slept.
That sounds terrible. Did it take you long to settle in?
About a month. The culture shock was not the language, it was the rhythm. Dinner at six, pubs closed early, and I was homesick every Sunday.
And the classes? My brother said the course load was heavier than at GV.
He is right. If I had gone to office hours in the first week, I would not have fallen behind in two classes.
And money? The stipend does not look very generous.
It is not. If I had learned to budget earlier, I would still have some savings now. Honestly, I spent too much in the first month.
Then I will learn from your mistakes. When you look back on it, was it worth it?
Completely. Just make the most of it, and take one elective that has nothing to do with law.

People ask me what I would change about my exchange year, and my answer surprises them. I would not choose a different city or a different university. I would change the first three weeks. I arrived thinking I would make friends in class, but in a big law school nobody talks in class. If I had joined a club in the first week, I would have met people much faster. The second thing is money. I did not budget, because the stipend looked like a lot in my currency, and by November I was eating pasta every night. And the third thing is the one I tell everyone. If you feel homesick, do not hide in your room. Go to one event, just one, even when you do not want to. That is how the culture shock ends.

Hello, this is a message for incoming exchange students from the university housing office. We have had a lot of questions, so here is the short version. Rooms on campus are allocated in order of application, and last year every room was taken by the end of May. If you apply after that, you will have to find private housing, which is usually more expensive and further from the law school. When you apply, please tell us if you would prefer a single room or a shared room with a roommate. Shared rooms cost about thirty percent less. And one more thing. Your stipend will not arrive before you do, so plan to cover your first month of rent yourself. If you have questions, our office hours are Monday to Thursday, from ten to four.
